mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in FEDFUNDS exceeds +0.25 percentage points, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive due to anticipation of accommodative monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 20-day returns during the prior 12-month period with similar FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to increased labor market uncertainty and wage stagnation.
failure_condition: In regimes where both PAYEMS and UNRATE are above average, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) after controlling for inflation and GDP momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals strengthening consumer demand momentum.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the 3-month HOUST growth is not sustained or is accompanied by negative GDP revisions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (≥10% monthly drop) coinciding with a positive 20-day change in GDPC1 suggests supply-side weakness that compresses equity valuations, producing negative forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change ≤ -10% and GDPC1 monthly change > +1%
failure_condition: In supply contraction regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines are not accompanied by strong demand signals (e.g., CPIAUCSL < 2% y/y).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS falls below 1% for two consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as investors anticipate further rate cuts and liquidity injection.
failure_condition: Over 12 months following the trigger, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently higher than the 60-day returns during the prior two months of FEDFUNDS > 1% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in PAYEMS and RSAFS by at least 5% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to heightened unemployment risk and reduced business hiring.
failure_condition: In contraction regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when other demand indicators (e.g., HOUST) are rising simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as lower unemployment is associated with stronger equity risk appetite.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 60-day return during the prior three months of UNRATE ≥ 3% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (≥2% month-over-month) accompanied by a 20-day negative return in S&P 500 futures implies that inflation surprise triggers a short-term risk-off reaction, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In inflation surprise regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL increases are not followed by persistent risk-off flows (e.g., FEDFUNDS remains steady).
